newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia trying to arrange Belarus compromise talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia trying to arrange Belarus compromise talks.

text.p: Top Russian officials, including the prime minister, may on Wednesday meet Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko and parliamentarians who want to impeach him, the speaker of Russia's lower house of parliament said.

Lukashenko, whom an increasingly concerned Russia urged on Tuesday to seek compromise with his opponents, has said he will decide by 1100 GMT whether to attend talks, possibly in the western Russian city of Smolensk, close to the Belarus border.

State Duma chairman Gennady Seleznyov told Russian deputies he hoped such talks, possibly involving Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, could defuse the political crisis in Belarus, which stands between Russia and central Europe.
"We must avoid sad consequences," he said.

Seleznyov and Yegor Stroyev, chairman of the Federation Council upper house, plan to meet the speaker of the Belarus Supreme Soviet, Semyon Sharetsky, a leader of parliamentary opposition to Lukashenko's plan to seek a popular mandate for sweeping new presidential powers in a referendum on Sunday.

The political standoff between the president on the one side and the parliamentary majority and constitutional court on the other has drawn comparisons with the situation in Russia in 1993, when President Boris Yeltsin resorted to force.
Last April, Yeltsin and Lukashenko agreed to form a two-state "community" with Belarus, the former Soviet state closest to Moscow.

Lukashenko, elected in 1994, wants to subsume Belarus in a greater Russia, but independence for Belarus brought by the break-up of the Soviet Union has stirred some nationalist feelings in the country of 10 million.
The Duma passed a resolution on Wednesday urging all sides to seek a compromise.
